test_policy.notes: CUNY-wide: test optional for undergraduate admission; first-year applicants may choose whether to submit SAT or ACT scores and the absence of scores cannot be used to deny admission. Baruch's page states the policy for 'Fall 2023 through Spring 2027 admission'; no end date for fall 2027 entry is given, so fall 2027 is not separately confirmed. The Common Data Set C8 lists SAT and ACT as 'not required, but considered if submitted'.

requirements.supplemental_essays: Essay recommended, not required, for freshman applicants (CUNY essay prompts: something meaningful not reflected in the application; a setback and what you learned; or any topic). Macaulay Honors College applicants submit two of three Macaulay essays.
requirements.notes: Apply with the CUNY application (not the Common App); one application can list up to 6 CUNY colleges with one fee; freshman fee $65. CUNY application fee waivers are for New York State applicants only. Letters of recommendation and the essay are recommended, not required. Documents go to CUNY, not to Baruch, and applications stay incomplete until the fee and all documents are received (allow 4-6 weeks for processing). Applicants educated outside the U.S. need the secondary-school record with English translations and, if they need an F-1/J-1 visa, a TOEFL, IELTS or PTE score; Baruch says the Duolingo English Test is accepted as an alternative. Baruch suggests international students send everything at least 4 weeks before the deadline. Decisions are rolling. The CDS lists 15 required academic units (4 English, 3 math, 2 science with lab, 2 language, 3 social studies, 1 visual or performing arts). Macaulay Honors College has its own binding early decision (Oct 26, 2026) and regular (Nov 16, 2026) deadlines; the pages do not say whether international students can receive Macaulay or Baruch Scholars awards.

deadlines.label: International first-year application deadline (fall 2027 entry)
deadlines.notes: Baruch and CUNY list December 1 as the application deadline for freshman applicants requesting a student visa or with full or partial credentials from outside the U.S. (U.S.-educated applicants: February 1 priority); admission is rolling from January to July. The page prints no year for these rows, but it gives Macaulay dates of October 26 and November 16, 2026, so it is the fall 2027 cycle. Baruch reviews applications after the priority deadline only as space allows.

deadlines.label: International supporting documents due (fall 2027 entry)
deadlines.notes: Transcripts and other supporting documents for international applicants, sent to CUNY.

english_policy.waiver_notes: Applicants on a temporary (F-1/J-1) visa who were educated in a non-English-speaking environment submit TOEFL, IELTS (Academic), PTE (Academic) or Duolingo scores; Baruch's page lists the Duolingo English Exam as an alternative. The undergraduate pages list no test exemptions. Scores are official when the testing agency sends them to CUNY or the CUNY code 2950 is listed when registering.

english.notes: Internet-based TOEFL, old 0-120 scale, from the CUNY comparison chart row for Baruch College (the highest minimum among CUNY senior colleges). The chart does not give a new 1-6 scale minimum.

aid.notes: Common Data Set H6 ticks that both institutional need-based and non-need-based scholarship and grant aid are available to degree-seeking nonresidents, with no recipient count or average award given. Baruch's scholarship page says most Baruch scholarships require the FAFSA and unmet need, that merit-only scholarships are rarely available, and that international students 'should not complete the FAFSA'; it does not say which awards international first-years can receive, and Baruch, Dean's and Macaulay scholars are chosen at admission. U.S. federal and New York State aid does not apply to F-1 students. F-1/J-1 students pay the nonresident tuition rate (CUNY 2026-27 page: $620 per credit).

sat.note: No SAT code is printed on the CUNY or Baruch pages checked; pick the college by name in the College Board search.

act.note: No ACT code is printed on the CUNY or Baruch pages checked; look it up at act.org.

toefl.note: CUNY-wide university code for official test score reports (CUNY How to Apply page).

ielts.note: No IELTS institution code is listed; the page says to have the testing agency send scores to CUNY.

duolingo.note: No Duolingo institution code is listed.

pte.note: No PTE institution code is listed.

tier_notes.general: Our estimate: 47.5% of fall 2024 applicants admitted, SAT middle 50% of 550-690 ERW and 550-710 Math for the 12% who submitted scores (Common Data Set), CUNY test-optional; placed with other large urban public commuter universities (Temple, Rutgers-Newark) at D+.
tier_notes.business: Our estimate, no ranking source checked: business is Baruch's core (College Navigator shows 2,543 bachelor's business completions, Zicklin School of Business), so it is placed a step above the general tier.
tier_notes.engineering: No engineering program (no bachelor's engineering programs in College Navigator).
